classification.difficultyReason: Plans conversions through a common currency before combining funds, then reframes a falling euro value as more euros per Australian dollar and therefore a steeper line.

content.prompt: Sandy travels to Europe via the USA. She uses this graph to calculate her currency conversions.

spec.sourceRegion: Currency conversion graph beneath question 8 shared stem
spec.description: Two straight conversion lines share axes. Labelled horizontal ticks are 0 to 100 in tens; labelled vertical ticks are 10 to 80 in tens, with minor ticks every 5. Dotted guides mark both conversion values at A$50 and A$100. The graph has no background grid.
spec.mathematics: US dollars = 0.75 × Australian dollars; euros = 0.6 × Australian dollars. Guide intersections are (50,37.5), (50,30), (100,75) and (100,60).
spec.answerVisibility: All axes, conversion lines, labels and dotted guides are permanent student-visible givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: After leaving the USA she has $\mathrm{US}\$150$ to add to the $\mathrm{A}\$600$ that she plans to spend in Europe. She converts all of her money to euros. How many euros does she have to spend in Europe?

answer.worked:
From the graph, A$\$100$ buys US$\$75$ and €60.
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{US}\$150\text{ in AUD} &= 150\times\frac{100}{75}\\
&= \mathrm{A}\$200\\
\text{Total AUD} &= 200+600\\
&= \mathrm{A}\$800\\
\text{Euros} &= 800\times\frac{60}{100}\\
&= 480
\end{aligned}$$
She has €480 to spend in Europe.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the value of the euro falls in comparison to the Australian dollar, what will be the effect on the gradient of the line used to convert Australian dollars to euros?

answer.short: The gradient increases; the line becomes steeper.
answer.worked: Each Australian dollar buys more euros. The gradient represents euros per Australian dollar, so the gradient increases and the line becomes steeper.
